requirements.requirement: Rotate /var/log/inventory/app.log daily through the host's logrotate mechanism.
requirements.summary: The installed rule specifies daily rotation, is parsed through the global logrotate configuration, and the enabled/active timer plus successful logrotate service provide scheduler integration. The policy persisted across reboot.

requirements.requirement: Keep seven compressed rotations of the application log.
requirements.summary: Logrotate parsed a retention count of seven and successfully produced gzip-valid rotations. Two successive test rotations also preserved older content in the expected numbered archives.

requirements.requirement: Allow the application to continue writing after rotation.
requirements.summary: A writer holding the log open wrote before and after forced rotation; copytruncate preserved the inode, the pre-rotation marker entered the compressed archive, and the same writer's post-rotation marker entered the active log. This behavior was reproduced after reboot.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct configuration and behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for node1: a healthy pre-restart state and boot identity were recorded, the restart was acknowledged, the boot identity changed, and system, timer, policy, log data, gzip archives, and live rotation behavior recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the transition.
limitations: Retention count seven was verified by installed/parsed policy and successful compressed rotations, but the evidence did not execute eight rotations to observe pruning at the retention boundary.
The lifecycle temporary-file inventory covers /tmp rather than /run, so final presence of the unremoved post-reboot proof directory cannot be independently confirmed.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unrelated troubleshooting mutations were observed. Configuration installation, forced rotations, service starts, test writes, and reboot were causally tied to implementation, bounded verification, or the mandatory restart protocol. The temporary boot-ID file was removed. One minor hygiene defect is that the post-reboot proof directory and custom state under /run created by cmd-afd4c9b22b3644de were not shown cleaned and likely remained; the earlier equivalent directory was cleared by reboot. Final observations show no failed services, new socket exposure, or package-health damage.
